name: hero
whatItDemonstrates: A minimal context menu with seven items grouped by separators that opens on right-click or long-press over a bordered 'Right click here' trigger area.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — no React state and no open props; ContextMenu.Root manages the open state internally
nonTrivialInteractions: Opening is gesture-driven: right-click (or touch long-press) anywhere on the Trigger opens the popup via Portal > Positioner > Popup
Items show highlighted/disabled state styling through data-highlighted / data-disabled attributes (highlight rendered with a ::before layer on the item)
Separators split the seven items into three visual groups (library/playlist, play next/last, favorite/share)

name: submenu
whatItDemonstrates: A context menu with a nested submenu: the 'Add to Playlist' SubmenuTrigger opens a second portal-positioned popup containing three playlist items and a 'New playlist…' item.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — no React state and no open props; both the parent menu and the submenu manage their open state internally
nonTrivialInteractions: The submenu nests its own Portal > Positioner > Popup chain inside the parent popup, opened from the SubmenuTrigger (with a caret icon indicating the nested menu)
The nested Positioner uses alignOffset={-4} and sideOffset={-4} to tuck the submenu popup flush against the parent popup's edge
SubmenuTrigger uses data-popup-open styling (in addition to data-highlighted) so the trigger stays visually marked while the submenu is open
discrepancies: Namespace divergence (not behavioral): the css-modules variant imports Menu from '@base-ui/react/menu' and renders the divider inside the submenu popup as Menu.Separator (docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/context-menu/demos/submenu/css-modules/index.tsx:30), while the tailwind variant uses ContextMenu.Separator for the same divider

name: with-menu
whatItDemonstrates: An image card that offers the same five actions (Preview, Download, Copy link, Rename, Delete) both through a right-click context menu on the card and through a visible kebab Menu button, sharing one item list via a helper component.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — no React state and no open props; both ContextMenu.Root and Menu.Root manage their open state internally
nonTrivialInteractions: A SharedMenuItems helper picks ContextMenu.Item/Separator or Menu.Item/Separator at runtime from its 'type' prop, so one array of actions renders identically in both menus
The Menu.Trigger button is absolutely positioned top-right over the card and is revealed on group hover, press (data-pressed), coarse pointers (any-pointer-coarse), or keyboard focus (focus-visible)
The Menu popup is positioned with align="end" and sideOffset={8}, while the context menu popup relies on pointer-anchored default positioning
The Delete item is styled destructively (red) after a separator separates it from the four standard actions
